items.title: fix(fleet-queue): claim by explicit id; pin claim lease + lane storage (#7617)
items.body: Closes #7617 ## What was wrong `verb_claim` (Turso queue broker) claimed a task via a subquery, then re-read the result as *"the newest claimed row for (queue, worker_id)"*. Every lane shares `worker_id = repo-worker-code`, so under concurrent claims that re-read can return **another lane's just-claimed task**: - the caller is handed a row stamped with a foreign `lane_id` — live repro this shift (2026-11-08): lane code-u claims returned task 13384 stamped `code-e` and task 8500 stamped `code-t`, claimed with `--lane code-u`; - the caller checkpoints/parks a task it does not own, and the claim guard in the same loop could quarantine a live foreign claim — a writer that displaces live claims, the #7617 failure family (task 11049's claim vanishing mid-work); - sibling lane-storage issue #7598 is the same re-read. The lease contract was also one literal away from the same class of bug: `2700` (claim default) and `900` (heartbeat extension default) were bare literals in different verbs. ## Fix - Pick the candidate **id first**, claim THAT row with a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND status IN ('queued','parked')` (status re-check keeps the claim atomic; a lost race re-picks), read the claimed row back **by id**. The `leases` row insert now provably names the same task the caller is handed. - Named constants `CLAIM_DEFAULT_LEASE_SECONDS = 2700` and `HEARTBEAT_DEFAULT_EXTEND_SECONDS = 900`; `claim_lease_until()` is the single source for the stored `lease_until` (tasks row and leases row), computed from one clock read with `claimed_at`. ## Regression tests (oracle: #7617 acceptance) - `claim_lease_is_the_requested_lease_not_the_heartbeat_default` — stored lease is claimed_at + requested lease (2700), never + the 900 s heartbeat default; the two defaults are pinned distinct. - `claim_lane_argument_is_stored_verbatim` — the lane passed at claim reaches the UPDATE verbatim; a lane-less claim stores NULL, never another lane's id. Verified on the laptop: `cargo test -p fleet-queue --features queue-broker --lib claim_` → 10 passed incl. both new tests; full `turso_queue` suite 20 passed. Queue task 14226. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(fleet-queue): lifecycle verbs refuse another lane's claim (#6985)
items.body: Before: every scheduled lane claims as the same worker, `repo-worker-code`, and the lifecycle verbs only checked the worker. So lane B could heartbeat, checkpoint, park or complete a task lane A held, and the overlap showed up only as two agent notes on the issue (#6985, task 12453 and others). After: `heartbeat`, `checkpoint`, `park`, `release`, `block`, `fail` and `complete` take `--lane ` (or `REPO_QUEUE_LANE` from the environment). When the row records the claiming lane and the caller names a different lane, the broker refuses with `task N is not claimed by repo-worker-code on lane code-b: lane code-a holds it` and writes a `claim_refused` event naming both lanes. How: `claimed_by` now takes the request and checks `foreign_lane_claim(row, req)` after the worker match. A missing lane on either side, or an execution mode (`direct`, `opencode`) in place of a lane id, keeps the old worker-only check, so callers that pass no lane behave as before. Lanes need to pass `--lane` (or export `REPO_QUEUE_LANE`) on these verbs to get the protection. The claim itself was already atomic per row (#7617). Tests: `lifecycle_verbs_refuse_another_lanes_claim_6985`, and the usage strings list the new flag. fleet-queue lib: 444 passed. Refs #6985 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01YLT5JyFdZgVpkFFqSHMPHV)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.body: Closes the remaining acceptance item of #7068 (claim race: task 11895, lanes code-m/code-f, 2026-11-08 — a losing `fleet queue claim` call returned the winner's live claim, lane stamp and all). ## What I found The mechanism was already fixed by #7617 (PR #7882): the early Turso claim shape re-read its result as "the newest claimed row for (queue, worker_id)" — with every lane sharing `repo-worker-code`, the loser was handed another lane's task. Current `verb_claim` picks a candidate id first, claims it with ONE conditional UPDATE that re-checks the full pick predicate, reads the row back **by id**, and re-picks on 0 affected rows; `claim_by_id` re-checks the observed status the same way. The Postgres `claim_repo_task` (migration-0023) uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` + `RETURNING` and never had the shape. What #7068 still lacked was acceptance item 2: **a regression test exercising two concurrent claims (distinct lane ids, same queue) showing exactly one winner per task.** This PR adds it — no behavior change. ## Changes (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs` only) - Extract the pick path's claim UPDATE into `claim_update_sql(pick_predicate)` — byte-identical statement — so its shape is pinnable in tests without a live store. - `claim_update_sql_rechecks_pick_eligibility_for_the_picked_id` — the UPDATE is keyed `WHERE id = ?` and re-checks status/attempts/not_before, so the loser's UPDATE matches 0 rows once the winner flips the row to `claimed`. - `claim_race_two_lanes_exactly_one_winner_per_task` — the task 11895 fixture: both lanes see the queued row claimable; after code-f's claim lands (status `claimed`, `lane_id = code-f`), the loser's claim view of that row is closed, and the next queued row stays claimable (loser moves on or gets no-task — never the winner's row). - `claim_paths_never_reread_a_workers_newest_claimed_row` — source oracle in the style of fleet-search's serve-contract tests: neither claim path may reintroduce a worker-keyed newest-claimed re-read; read-back stays by row id. ## Tests - `cargo test -p fleet-queue --features queue-broker` — **125 passed, 0 failed** (18 claim-filtered, including the 3 new tests). - Note: `cargo fmt --check` reports pre-existing drift across this crate under the current toolchain; this change follows the file's existing style and does not reformat unrelated code. Queue: task 14493 (repo-health-code-pilot), lane code-k. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
